critique: The black background, luminous amber particle color, and dense filament/dot rendering are convincing. Frame 1 is relatively compact, but it reads as a folded rosette with multiple rolled lobes rather than a unified liquid drop. By frame 4 it breaks into a tall, stringy turbulent plume with separated curls and a porous interior. The motion is substantially too violent and deforming for the intended cohesive Single Drop behavior.

suggestions.why: Reducing the very strong X fluid flow will prevent the compact mass from shearing into the broad, vertically ragged plume seen at t4.
Lower vortex strength so the particle field retains one rounded core instead of repeatedly rolling into distinct lobes and protruding tendrils.
Reduce random X swirl, which is contributing to the broken outer contour and detached-looking curls.
Reduce random Y swirl to keep the drop compact rather than stretching it into a tall irregular mass over time.
